title: Geo-tagged KMS routing and RBACv2 policy converter with adaptive audit sampling
author: Sana Park
release_notes: Added geo-tagged KMS routing that respects dataset residency tags; introduced a policy-converter CLI to migrate RBACv1 flat bindings to RBACv2 attribute-based bindings; enabled adaptive audit sampling (configurable default with high-risk triggers).
description:
Context & motivation: Customers with strict data residency requirements ask for region-scoped key routing and clear audit trail semantics across Redwood deployments. Existing RBAC v1 flat bindings and global KMS selection made it hard to enforce region pinning for keys and to reason about access in multi-tenant setups. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) a geo-tagged KMS routing layer that selects customer KMS endpoints based on resource residency tags and key origin policies, 2) an RBACv2 policy-converter tool and migration path to convert legacy bindings into attribute-driven role bindings (resource.affiliation and request.location attributes), and 3) an adaptive audit-sampling heuristic that preserves full capture for high-risk flows while sampling high-volume benign traffic to keep retention costs reasonable.
Summary of changes:
- runtime: add KmsRegionResolver and routing policy hooks that check resource.tags.residency and key_origin metadata to choose KMS endpoints with explicit failure modes (reject, fallback-to-tenant-default, or buffered-encrypt for delayed routing).
- policy: add new RBAC schema fields (attribute_selectors, affinity_rules) and evaluator changes to match attribute-based checks during authorization.
- tooling: new CLI `redwood policy-convert --input old_bindings.json --output rbacv2.json` that performs conservative, reviewed translations and emits a migration report.
- audit: add sampling controller that uses dynamic rules: sample_rate default 0.1 for high-volume read-only ops, full_capture for operations touching sensitive tags (e.g., residency:EU, pii:true, kms_origin:customer), and short-term burst-exemption for new keys.
- data migrations: add SQL migration to policy_store (v38 -> v39) to create attributes column and backfill affiliation hints for tenants that opt-in.
- tests: unit tests for resolver logic, e2e scenario tests for policy-convert output, integration test verifying audit sampling behavior under synthetic load.
Checklist:
- [x] KmsRegionResolver implementation and unit tests
- [x] RBACv2 schema changes and evaluator unit tests
- [x] policy-convert CLI + integration tests
- [x] SQL migration and reversible migration script
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented
- [x] Updated docs (security/compliance) and warning banner for opt-in migration
How to validate locally:
- run `make dev` and start `redwood-local` with feature flag `FEATURE_GEO_KMS=true`
- run `./bin/redwood policy-convert --input testdata/old_bindings.json --output /tmp/new_policy.json` and inspect migration report in `/tmp/new_policy.json.report`
- run `curl -H \"X-Resource-Residency: eu-west-1\" ...` against the canary endpoint to exercise routed KMS calls
Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag with migration scripts and CLI. 2) Enable geo routing in dedicated canary region for a small set of tenants (opt-in). 3) Run conversion tool on an opt-in test tenant and validate behavior for 72h. 4) Gradually expand and enable adaptive audit-sampling defaults.
Backwards compatibility notes:
- By default the system falls back to previous behavior (tenant-default KMS) unless tenant opts into residency enforcement.
- Policy-convert emits human-reviewable recommendations; it does not auto-apply changes.
- Migration script is reversible and included as part of this PR.
Performance considerations:
- Resolver caches region->endpoint lookup with TTL and leverages existing routing cache; worst-case added latency on first key route is ~12ms in our benchmarks.
- Audit sampling reduces storage rate to keep overall ingestion cost neutral for high-traffic tenants.
Security review summary:
- We validated that encrypted envelopes remain tenant-scoped; the routing layer only affects which KMS service is called and never exposes plaintext.
- KMS calls include an additional signature header X-KMS-Route-Proof for cross-region routing audits.
Documentation: docs/security/kms-routing.md and docs/security/rbacv2-migration.md included. Related work items: ENG-8472 (policy migration), SEC-421 (compliance review).
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial resolver implementation; add RBACv2 schema and evaluator tests; add policy-convert CLI and conversion tests; SQL migration and backfill; documentation and canary rollout notes.
discussion:
Ethan Liu: Can the resolver be configured to reject when region tag is missing?
Sana Park: Yes - config options include 'enforce'|'fallback'|'warn'. Default is 'fallback' to tenant default to avoid accidental denial.
Priya Joshi: Policy-convert looks great; ensure we don't over-assign broad roles during translation.
Sana Park: The converter attaches a 'review_recommendation' array with suggested tighter attribute selectors; the default output is conservative (keeps original permissions, adds attribute selectors as recommendations, not enforced).
Liam O'Neill: Any risk of metadata injection in tags?
Sana Park: We added validation on tag shape and a strict whitelist for recognized residency keys during resolution; unknown tags are ignored by resolver and produce a warning audit event.
Ethan Liu: CI showed a flaky test initially?
Sana Park: Fixed a time-based race in kms_resolver_test by stubbing cache TTL; CI now green.
Priya Joshi: Approved after small nits on docs formatting.
Mergebot: Squash merged by Sana Park.
